title: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis: granular C3 (and IgG) deposits
vignette: An 8-year-old boy is brought to the office due to acute facial puffiness. His mother reports that for the preceding 24 hours he has been easily fatigued and has had dark urine. The patient was treated for a skin infection 3 weeks ago but has no chronic medical conditions. Temperature is 36.1 C (97 F) and blood pressure is 140/94 mm Hg. Physical examination shows periorbital edema and mild pitting edema along the ankles. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A representative renal biopsy sample is shown in the image, demonstrating coarse, granular ('lumpy-bumpy') immunofluorescent deposits along the glomerular basement membrane and mesangium. The fluorescent areas on the slide most likely indicate the presence of which of the following substances?

clues.note: Dark (cola-colored) urine indicates hematuria - a hallmark of the nephritic syndrome of poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.

clues.text: treated for a skin infection 3 weeks ago
clues.note: A nephritogenic group A Streptococcus infection (skin or pharynx) 1-3 weeks earlier is the classic trigger for poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
Hypertension (with edema and hematuria) completes the nephritic picture of poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.

clues.text: coarse, granular ('lumpy-bumpy') immunofluorescent deposits along the glomerular basement membrane and mesangium
clues.note: Granular ('lumpy-bumpy') deposits of IgG, IgM, and C3 on the GBM/mesangium are the immunofluorescence hallmark of poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.

whatMatters: Nephritic syndrome (edema, hematuria, hypertension) ~1-3 weeks after a streptococcal skin infection in a child = poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis. Immunofluorescence shows GRANULAR ('lumpy-bumpy') deposits of IgG, IgM, and C3. Of the options, the fluorescent deposits represent C3. Answer C.
strategy: Recognize poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, then recall its immunofluorescence: granular immune-complex deposits containing IgG/IgM and, notably, C3 (activated via the ALTERNATE complement pathway, so C1q/C4 are typically absent). Among the choices, C3 is the deposit. Reject C1q (classic pathway - not typical), albumin (lost in urine, not deposited), fibrin (crescents of RPGN), IgE (type I allergy), and M protein (streptococcal wall antigen, not found in the deposits).

eliminations.label: Albumin - lost in urine, not deposited
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the major plasma protein; in glomerular disease it leaks into the urine. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: albumin doesn't form immune deposits on the GBM; the granular fluorescence is immunoglobulin/complement. ✅ Correct if: asking what's lost in nephrotic-range proteinuria.

eliminations.label: C1q - classic pathway (usually absent here)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: C1q is a classical-complement-pathway component (seen in lupus nephritis 'full house'). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis activates the ALTERNATE pathway, so deposits contain C3 but rarely C1q/C4. ✅ Correct if: lupus nephritis (C1q-positive).

eliminations.label: Fibrin - crescents of RPGN
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: fibrin deposition in Bowman space forms the crescents of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this is the granular immune-complex pattern of poststreptococcal GN, not crescentic fibrin. ✅ Correct if: crescentic (rapidly progressive) glomerulonephritis.

eliminations.label: IgE - type I hypersensitivity (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: IgE mediates type I (allergic) reactions. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: poststreptococcal GN is a type III immune-complex disease (IgG/IgM + C3), not IgE-mediated. ✅ Correct if: allergy/atopy or parasitic disease.

eliminations.label: M protein - streptococcal antigen, not in deposits
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: streptococcal M protein is a cell-wall antiphagocytic virulence factor (linked to rheumatic fever via myosin cross-reactivity). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: M protein is not the substance found in the glomerular immune deposits of poststreptococcal GN. ✅ Correct if: rheumatic heart disease pathogenesis.

reasoning: Nephritic syndrome (edema, hematuria, hypertension) ~1-3 weeks after a strep skin infection = poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
It is a type III immune-complex disease depositing on the GBM/mesangium
Immunofluorescence shows granular ('lumpy-bumpy') IgG, IgM, and C3 (alternate complement pathway)
-> the fluorescent deposits are C3; answer C
mechanism: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) is the most common cause of pediatric nephritic syndrome, occurring 1-3 weeks after infection of the pharynx or SKIN with a nephritogenic strain of group A Streptococcus. Streptococcal antigens and host antibodies form IMMUNE COMPLEXES that deposit in the glomerular basement membrane and mesangium (type III hypersensitivity) and activate complement predominantly via the ALTERNATE pathway. On immunofluorescence, this yields coarse, GRANULAR ('LUMPY-BUMPY') deposits of IgG, IgM, and C3; electron microscopy shows subepithelial 'humps.' Because complement is activated (and consumed), serum C3 is typically LOW during the acute phase, and the deposits characteristically contain C3 (with little/no C1q or C4, distinguishing PSGN from lupus nephritis's 'full house'). Clinically: cola-colored urine (hematuria), periorbital/peripheral edema, and hypertension; most children recover fully. Among the listed substances, the fluorescent granular deposits represent C3 (and immunoglobulin) - not albumin (lost in urine), fibrin (crescents), IgE (allergy), or M protein (a streptococcal cell-wall antigen not found in the deposits).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Renal > poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis: nephritic syndrome 1-3 wk post-strep (throat/skin); granular ('lumpy-bumpy') IgG/IgM/C3 on IF; subepithelial humps on EM; low C3 (alternate pathway).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Granular immune-complex deposits in PSGN contain C3 (and IgG) - not C1q, albumin, or fibrin.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on nephritic syndrome, immunofluorescence, granular vs linear deposits, alternate complement pathway, or subepithelial humps? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: C1q = lupus (classic pathway); albumin = urine loss; fibrin = crescents (RPGN); IgE = allergy; M protein = strep antigen (not in deposits).

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On immunofluorescence: coarse, granular ('lumpy-bumpy') fluorescent deposits speckle the glomerular basement membrane and mesangium. Anchor: 'granular immune deposits = immune-complex GN (PSGN) = IgG + C3.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: PSGN = granular IgG/IgM/C3 (lumpy-bumpy), subepithelial humps, low C3 (alternate pathway); 1-3 wk post-strep.

keywords.front: Nephritic syndrome ~1-3 weeks after strep skin/throat infection

firstAid.detail: Renal: granular IgG/IgM/C3 (lumpy-bumpy), subepithelial humps; low C3.

memoryHook: Weeks after strep, the kidney lights up 'lumpy-bumpy' with immune junk - IgG and C3 - while serum C3 drops: poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
